newsitem.title: CHINA: China says no foreign buying of A shares soon.
newsitem.headline: China says no foreign buying of A shares soon.

text.p: China will not allow foreign investment in the domestic A share market anytime soon, People's Bank of China vice governor Chen Yaoxian said on Thursday.
"The A share market cannot be opened up all of a sudden," the central bank official told a business conference.
China is currently studying plans for joint venture investment funds, and several foreign securities firms have been preparing for the possible move.
Speculation of such investment has periodically bolstered the domestic stock markets.
The People's Bank of China official said that the regulatory framework had to be put in place and domestic investors needed a better idea of market risk before such investment could be permitted.
A shares are currently reserved for domestic investors while foreign currency denominated B shares are supposed to be for foreign investors.
